holding_summary: A clause requiring the tenant to forfeit the entire deposit upon any breach, without proportionality, was held to be an unreasonable penalty under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act.
A deposit exceeding ten months' rent was reduced by the forum to two months' rent, consistent with the Karnataka Rent Act limit.
A 30-day mutual notice period was upheld as reasonable and consistent with established landlord-tenant practice under the Delhi Rent Act.
A clause providing only 3 days' notice for termination was held to be unconscionable and contrary to the Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017.
A lock-in period penalty clause imposing 6 months' rent on early departure was reduced to 2 months as a reasonable measure of the landlord's re-letting costs.
A clause permitting the landlord to enter the property 'at any time without prior notice' was held to violate the tenant's right to peaceful enjoyment.
A clause shifting all structural repair obligations to the tenant, including damage caused by natural wear, was voided as it contradicted the landlord's statutory duty under applicable rent law.
A mutual termination clause with 60 days' notice was upheld as fair and consistent with the Maharashtra Rent Control Act requirements.
A unilateral termination right granted solely to the landlord, with no corresponding right for the tenant, was held to be an unconscionable term.
An arbitration clause selecting an arbitrator 'to be appointed solely by the landlord' was modified by the court to require a neutral arbitrator under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
A blanket prohibition on subletting without landlord consent was upheld as a standard and reasonable restriction.
A clause imposing a compound interest penalty of 24% per annum on delayed rent was reduced to simple interest at the applicable statutory rate as excessive.
A clause permitting the landlord to enter with 48 hours' written notice for inspection was upheld as reasonable.
Interest on security deposit withheld beyond 30 days of vacating was ordered to be paid at the bank savings rate.
A clause requiring the tenant to maintain interior surfaces and minor fixtures was upheld as a reasonable allocation of day-to-day maintenance costs.
